items.title: Robert Pattinson Says The Batman Part 2's Fight Scenes Are 'Significantly Harder' to Perform
items.description: Robert Pattinson says his age is making it harder to perform the fight scenes in The Batman Part 2.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Robert Pattinson says his age is making it harder to perform the fight scenes in The Batman Part 2.

The actor spoke with GQ ahead of the release of his new movie, Primetime, and naturally was asked about returning to the role of Batman. Pattinson noted that although the experience has been good and he's excited about the film, he's having a 'significantly harder' time with the fight scenes due to the large gap between movies.

“I’m definitely feeling my age when fighting a lot," said Pattinson. "I’m literally like, ‘Goddamn, this is significantly harder than it used to be.’ But it’s really fun. And I think the movie’s going to be pretty great. It’s got a really, really fun cast, but it’s a marathon.”

Pattinson was cast as Batman in 2019, when he was 33 years old. He shot the film throughout 2020 and 2021, meaning it's been roughly five years since he last put on the cape and cowl. Ironically, part of the conceit of Pattinson's take on Batman was that he'd be a younger and more inexperienced version of the reluctant hero. However, the long wait for a sequel means Pattinson is older than Christian Bale was in The Dark Knight Rises and just three years younger than Ben Affleck was in Batman v Superman. Those two takes on the character were meant to be older and more broken down versions of the character.

It has been a long journey to get cameras rolling on The Batman Part 2, but things finally came together earlier this summer. The film will boast an incredibly impressive cast with the likes of Scarlett Johansson, Sebastian Stan, and Brian Tyree Henry all being tapped for a variety of roles, though they're largely being kept under wraps. A variety of set photos and videos have been popping up on social media for the last few months, showing intense action scenes in a snow-covered Gotham City.

The Batman Part 2 has had a variety of release dates over the years and was originally meant to release in October 2027 when production began. Unfortunately, the team behind the film opted to push it to a February 2028 release, so it will be a while before we see the Caped Crusader back on the big screen.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Avengers: Secret Wars Adds Noah Jupe to Highly Secretive Cast
items.description: Avengers: Secret Wars has added Noah Jupe to its cast in an undisclosed role.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Avengers: Secret Wars has added Noah Jupe to its cast in an undisclosed role.

According to Deadline, Jupe has been tapped to join the cast of one of the biggest movies on the horizon ahead of a shoot date later this year. The role is expected to play a "key part" in the story of the film. Absolutely no details were provided on who he's playing, but that doesn't mean we can't speculate, right? The most immediate guess is he's part of the new X-Men cast. Marvel announced a bunch of members of the next X-Men film at D23, which includes Sadie Sink, Adam Driver, Kit Connor, Inde Navarrette, and a handful of other up-and-coming stars.

Jupe is 21 years old, which means he would fit in quite well with the other X-Men cast members. He also starred alongside Sadie Sink in a stage version of Romeo and Juliet earlier this year. However, there are a lot of questions over whether the new X-Men will even be in Secret Wars. If Jupe isn't part of the X-Men, he could be a character like Nova, who is getting his own standalone film in the future. It's anyone's guess right now, and given that Marvel tried to keep Sadie Sink's role in Spider-Man: Brand New Day under wraps up until release, we may not know until the film comes to theaters in December 2027.

Noah Jupe has made a name for himself with the Quiet Place franchise, Hamnet, and a number of other high-profile projects. He's the first person to be formally cast in Secret Wars, as we're not sure who will survive Avengers: Doomsday and appear in the sequel. It seems like a safe bet to imagine Robert Downey Jr. will return as Doctor Doom and the likes of Chris Hemsworth and Chris Evans will return as Thor and Captain America respectively, but beyond that, it's hard to say. Evans has already teased a "brutal" story for Cap in Doomsday, but it's unclear what that looks like at the moment.

Avengers: Infinity War killed half of its cast, meaning most of the characters didn't return until the third act of Endgame. It wouldn't be surprising if the returning X-Men cast from the Fox-era films are killed off in Doomsday, but Marvel will likely keep all of this under wraps until it releases. Either way, the Marvel universe appears to be expanding in exciting ways.

items.title: Resident Evil 2 Director Hideki Kamiya Says Capcom Has Grown 'Numb' To How Scary New RE Games Are
items.description: Hideki Kamiya has confirmed that he was “not joking” when he begged Capcom to make a less-scary version of Resident Evil Requiem for the faint of heart, even arguing that the company has become "numb" to how frightening the newer games have gotten.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Hideki Kamiya has confirmed that he was “not joking” when he begged Capcom to make a less-scary version of Resident Evil Requiem for the faint of heart, even arguing that the company has become "numb" to how frightening the newer games have gotten.

In March 2026, Clovers Inc. — Kamiya’s newest game development studio — uploaded a video showing the team playing Resident Evil Requiem. Kamiya stood off to the side as one of his employees got to a cutscene near the beginning of the game, where he complained that, “I've been saying for forever, they should make a 'non-scary' mode.”

He said as much in a tweet around that same time, suggesting an alternate mode where “the zombies get all cute, the blood splatters turn into cherry blossom petals, the music becomes this upbeat, feel-good kind of tune, and you can just purely enjoy the puzzles and battles in a fun mood.”

We’re all playing Resident Evil Requiem!
Kamiya—who hates horror games—is doing his usual grumbling 🤭🍀 pic.twitter.com/ocbW8tsnDR

— CLOVERS Inc. (@CLOVERS_en) March 10, 2026

Kamiya doubled down on this request in an August interview with Video Games Chronicle, saying he was “one hundred percent serious” about it and even claimed that Capcom is going too far with how scary its Resident Evil games have gotten lately.

“Nowadays, with how photorealistic and high-fidelity video games have gotten, the amount of crazy, horrifying things that people are able to put on the screen is absolutely insane, and I think anybody who’s on the Resident Evil teams at Capcom, at this point, they must all be completely numb to how scary the thing they’re making is,” he told the outlet.

“This is not a joke; I’m being one hundred percent serious when I say that I wish they would make it so that their games can also be enjoyed by people like me, who can’t handle scary games at all.”

Kamiya said he wanted to revisit the Raccoon City Police Department in Requiem to see how Capcom handled the iconic area that he first created in the original Resident Evil 2 — but it was just too scary for him.

“I mean, just recently this year we had Resident Evil Requiem and the big return of Leon Kennedy, and he went back to Raccoon City, and he’s reliving all of those memories and all of those experiences. As somebody who directed that original game, Resident Evil 2, I was curious to know how that panned out for him. I wanted to experience that myself as a player, but the game was way too scary, and I couldn’t,” he said.

He went on to state that he’s requested changes to how scary the RE games are directly to the series’ developers and producers — usually to stunned reactions.

“And so, it’s not a joke. I legitimately wished it would include some kind of non-horror mode for people like me, because I talk to folks who are on the Resident Evil teams at Capcom just privately, and I tell them that their games are way too scary, and they’re like, ‘What? Come on, they’re not that scary.’ They seriously seem to have no awareness of how scary the things they make actually are, so I really hope they address that at some point.”

“I mean, it doesn’t even have to be anything super elaborate. You could just make it so that the zombies’ faces aren’t so scary. Why not have a mode that just puts, like, brown paper bags on all of their heads, or instead of having these dark, dingy rooms everywhere, they could have really pleasant mood lighting. I think even just making a few tweaks like those, it would make it so that somebody like me could make it all the way through the games. Oh, and no blood!”

“Which is precisely why I don’t think the teams at Capcom fully understand how scary the games that they’re making actually are!” He continued. “I told [series producer] Takeuchi-san to his face, ‘Your games are too scary!’ And he was like, ‘What? Seriously?!’ I get codes for every new Resident Evil when it comes out and it always comes with an email saying, ‘Hey, we hope you enjoy the game!’ And I’ll send back an email thanking them for the code, and say, ‘Well, I’d love to play the game, but unfortunately it’s too scary for me, so I’m not going to be able to,’ they come back with, ‘Oh, come on, it’s not that scary, you can do it!’”

Kamiya even joked that he’d make a spinoff game where Leon finally gets to enjoy a peaceful retirement, where players would take him “fishing in the countryside, foraging for wild veggies, baking bread, walking the dog,” etc.

Unfortunately for him, it doesn’t look like Capcom is going to take his notes into consideration, as a remake of Code Veronica and all its terrifying zombie combat is set to release next year.

items.title: GTA 6 Extended Look Tops Netflix Top 10 Chart in First Week
items.description: Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look dominated Netflix's top 10 chart in its first week (in the English Film category), racking up 31.1 million views in its first week, beating the second-place film on the list, the Robert DeNiro, Adam Scott, and Michelle Monaghan thriller The Whisper Man, which pulled in 23.2 million views. Worth noting is that GTA 6 handily beat its Netflix competition despite not debuting until Thursday.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look dominated Netflix's top 10 chart in its first week (in the English Film category), racking up 31.1 million views in its first week, beating the second-place film on the list, the Robert DeNiro, Adam Scott, and Michelle Monaghan thriller The Whisper Man, which pulled in 23.2 million views. Worth noting is that GTA 6 handily beat its Netflix competition despite not debuting until Thursday. The reporting period was from August 24-30. All data comes directly from Netflix.

The streamer notes that, "Netflix counts a 'view' as one full-runtime equivalent of watch time. Netflix defines a view as the total hours viewed for a title divided by its runtime. So one household watching a 27-minute video twice looks the same in Netflix's math as two households each watching it once." They no doubt mention this since YouTube counts a view the moment a video starts to play, and so far, on Rockstar's official YouTube channel, the GTA 6 Extended Look has 17 million views as of 12pm PT when this story published.

On the TV side, Death of the Pastor's Wife (19m views) took the top spot on last week's Netflix Top 10, and Facing El Chapo (20.7m views) topped the non-English film category.

And as it turns out, Rockstar approached Netflix about this Extended Look premiere, not the other way around. For a whole lot more on GTA 6, check out our report of what we got to see at Rockstar North that wasn't on Netflix, why significant others are already mad about Rockstar's imminent crime epic, confirmation on a lack of microtransactions at launch, 99 new details we spotted in the extended look, and so much more.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

items.title: Peter Cullen’s Final Optimus Prime Performance Confirmed for New Transformers Short
items.description: The late Peter Cullen's final voice performance as Optimus Prime will debut in a new animated short alongside select 40th anniversary Transformers: The Movie screenings.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
The late Peter Cullen’s final vocal performance as Optimus Prime will be in a new animated short film, Optimus Prime: Awakening, that will be presented following select 40th anniversary screenings of The Transformers: The Movie.

Hasbro and Fathom Entertainment announced the short film Tuesday:

“Optimus Prime: Awakening is a fully realized, 12-minute animated short designed as a love letter to the Transformers community and the late Peter Cullen, the legendary talent and voice of Optimus Prime. Optimus Prime: Awakening builds on the acclaimed storytelling and visuals of The Transformers: The Movie (1986), giving audiences the rare opportunity to experience the iconic cultural moment from the franchise’s past while exploring its future on the big screen.”

Hasbro and Fathom said, “Peter’s performance [in Optimus Prime: Awakening] reveals a deeper vulnerability while retaining the unmistakable strength and authority that made his portrayal iconic.”

Check out the key art for Optimus Prime: Awakening below.

Frank Welker, who voices Optimus Prime’s archenemy Megatron in the film, praised his late co-star in a statement:

“Optimus Prime and Megatron were made for each other. After all, one needs the perfect hero against the epitome of evil to create great drama. Peter’s portrayal of Prime was born of his own personal beliefs; honesty, loyalty, and always insisting on doing the right thing. This made it easy to be friends. Returning as Megatron and Soundwave for one final story opposite Peter’s Optimus in Optimus Prime: Awakening was a real gift. I will miss my friend, but that voice and his heart and values will always be part of Optimus Prime.”

Peter Cullen died August 26 at the age of 85.

The Transformers: The Movie returns to theatres internationally in 4K from September 17–22, 2026. Fathom has just announced new screenings in France, Singapore, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama and Peru.

Fans can also now pre-order The Transformers: The Movie 40th Anniversary Limited-Edition steelbook, which will be available on November 17 in both 4K UHD and Blu-ray.

items.title: Sony Rolls Out New Customer Harassment Policy After Physical Disc Controversy Sparks Backlash
items.description: Sony Japan has introduced a new customer harassment policy following widespread backlash toward its decision to stop producing physical game discs starting January 2028.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Sony Japan has introduced a new customer harassment policy following widespread backlash toward its decision to stop producing physical game discs starting January 2028.

Sony Japan published this policy on its official website on September 1, 2026, where it outlined several examples of harassment and urged customers to honor its behavioral guidelines.

“Our company strives to provide honest service so that our customers can use our products and services with peace of mind, and we value customer feedback to improve our services,” it wrote. “On the other hand, the dignity and safety of our employees must not be threatened by customer harassment, such as words or demands from customers that exceed what is considered reasonable according to social norms.”

Sony went on to say that it takes a “firm stance” against such behavior, which includes examples like “persistent and repeated, or prolonged, demands, excessive or unreasonable demands for compensation or apologies, and abusive language, threats, slander, and other similar behaviors.”

Other examples included “forcing someone to prostrate themselves” and “visiting our offices or related facilities without permission.” If any such behavior is confirmed, Sony says it may “restrict or suspend customer service” to protect its employees — and, if necessary, contact “police, lawyers, etc.” to take legal action or begin criminal proceedings against them.

Sony is one of several Japanese companies implementing such measures to protect their employees. In October 2025, a new law was enacted that required employers across the country to take action to prevent harassment toward their workers by customers. As told by Uni Global Union, this marked a massive shift in Japan's workplace culture, pivoting from a “customer is always right” mentality to a focus on worker protections.

Sony's policy hasn’t come out of the blue; the company has borne the brunt of backlash from angry players following its decision to stop making physical game discs, along with its divisive response to an ongoing lawsuit as a result of this strategy.

In August, Sony responded to a class action lawsuit that accused it of failing to clearly state that players are merely purchasing a revocable license when they buy a game on its digital store, arguing that “in the digital age, it is not plausible to allege that reasonable consumers believed they were obtaining ‘ownership’ of a digital game.”

A Dutch consumer group and the Stop Killing Games movement have also banded together to sue Sony, alleging that the company charged Dutch customers more on its digital store than buyers located elsewhere in the world.

The PlayStation store is at the center of another lawsuit against Sony in Mexico, where lawmakers argue that the company is engaging in “anti-competitive practices” by limiting purchases to its digital storefront, crippling competition from other games retailers.

Sony, for its part, is continuing to pursue an all-digital future, with chief financial officer Lin Tao saying it will "cautiously move this forward" with its plan to kill off game discs despite “strong views” from players.

“Our company strives to provide honest service so that our customers can use our products and services with peace of mind, and we value customer feedback to improve our services,” it wrote. “On the other hand, the dignity and safety of our employees must not be threatened by customer harassment, such as words or demands from customers that exceed what is considered reasonable according to social norms.”

Sony went on to say that it takes a “firm stance” against such behavior, which includes examples like “persistent and repeated, or prolonged, demands, excessive or unreasonable demands for compensation or apologies, and abusive language, threats, slander, and other similar behaviors.”

Other examples included “forcing someone to prostrate themselves” and “visiting our offices or related facilities without permission.” If any such behavior is confirmed, Sony says it may “restrict or suspend customer service” to protect its employees — and, if necessary, contact “police, lawyers, etc.” to take legal action or begin criminal proceedings against them.

Sony is one of several Japanese companies implementing such measures to protect their employees. In October 2025, a new law was enacted that required employers across the country to take action to prevent harassment toward their workers by customers. As told by Uni Global Union, this marked a massive shift in Japan's workplace culture, pivoting from a “customer is always right” mentality to a focus on worker protections.

Sony's policy hasn’t come out of the blue; the company has borne the brunt of backlash from angry players following its decision to stop making physical game discs, along with its divisive response to an ongoing lawsuit as a result of this strategy.

In August, Sony responded to a class action lawsuit that accused it of failing to clearly state that players are merely purchasing a revocable license when they buy a game on its digital store, arguing that “in the digital age, it is not plausible to allege that reasonable consumers believed they were obtaining ‘ownership’ of a digital game.”

A Dutch consumer group and the Stop Killing Games movement have also banded together to sue Sony, alleging that the company charged Dutch customers more on its digital store than buyers located elsewhere in the world.

The PlayStation store is at the center of another lawsuit against Sony in Mexico, where lawmakers argue that the company is engaging in “anti-competitive practices” by limiting purchases to its digital storefront, crippling competition from other games retailers.

Sony, for its part, is continuing to pursue an all-digital future, with chief financial officer Lin Tao saying it will "cautiously move this forward" with its plan to kill off game discs despite “strong views” from players.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass September 2026 Wave 1 Lineup Announced
items.description: Microsoft has announced the Xbox Game Pass September 2027 Wave 1 lineup, and it includes a Call of Duty blockbuster.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Microsoft has announced the Xbox Game Pass September 2027 Wave 1 lineup, and it includes a Call of Duty blockbuster.

Available today on all major Game Pass tiers, Shelldiver is an incremental game about a senior turtle trying to start a business selling jellyfish. It sounds odd, but its Steam reviews look promising, so maybe this is one worth hauling in.

Later this week, Speedrunners 2: King of Speed launches straight into Game Pass, bringing a second helping of competitive co-op platforming action. Game Pass premium members also gain access to Dice a Million, the roguelike deck builder already on other tiers.

Perhaps this batch's biggest inclusion is Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War, which is the Raven Software-made instalment that arrived back in 2020. We gave the game's single-player a 7/10 in our campaign review, though its multiplayer modes lagged behind that a little. There have been better CODs, in other words, though there have also been worse.

Later this month sees the addition of The Royal Writ, another roguelike deck builder, though this time with a medieval twist. Then there's Virtua Fighter 5, or Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage, to give its full name. "The World Stage" refers to its single-player "journey", though its bone-shattering multiplayer modes remain the star.

Last but not least, there's the previously-confirmed inclusion of Runescape: Dragonwilds, the first standalone title in Jagex’s long-running medieval MMORPG franchise. Dragonwilds has already shifted over 1 million copies during early access, so its open world, co-op, crafting and survival gameplay is obviously doing something right.

  • Shelldiver (Cloud, Console, and PC) — September 1, Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass
  • Speedrunners 2: King of Speed (Cloud, Xbox Series X/S, and PC) – September 3, Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass

items.title: Rockstar Games Reveals Its Official GTA Online Roleplaying Server, nopixel V
items.description: Rockstar Games has revealed its official GTA Online roleplaying server, nopixel V, ahead of GTA 6's launch.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Rockstar Games has revealed its official GTA Online roleplaying server, nopixel V, ahead of GTA 6's launch.

Grand Theft Auto 5 is one of the most popular games of all time, and part of that is thanks to major community support. In the late 2010s and early 2020s, modders went particularly crazy with the foundation Rockstar created and utilized it for roleplaying servers, such as the extremely popular nopixel. Rockstar has embraced this side of the community, acquiring the team behind the FiveM modding platform and collaborating with nopixel itself.

Now, nopixel is gearing up to release the next iteration of its roleplaying server, which will be officially supported by Rockstar Games. The two teamed up to produce a much richer and deeper roleplaying experience that will feature a reworked character customization system, enhanced graphics, and a wealth of quality of life changes. Perhaps the most notable thing for longtime GTA fans is that the Mile High Club, a building that has been under construction since the game's very first reveal trailer in 2011, has been finished exclusively for nopixel. The building is now a hotel and casino for roleplayers.

The server will be available directly through Rockstar's official launcher, meaning you won't have to tinker with any third-party tools or platforms, and players will be able to see it in action on September 8 when a bunch of the top RP streamers will be let loose on the streets of Los Santos. You can click here to check out a trailer, which showcases the depth and uniqueness of this new GTA experience.

Of course, many fans are likely going to wonder what this means for GTA 6. Rockstar Games has yet to make any kind of comments or announcement on the next iteration of GTA Online, but it would be shocking if there wasn't an online mode for GTA 6 later down the line. The single-player of GTA 6 is already a very roleplay-intensive experience, so it seems like Rockstar may be designing the game with a roleplay future in mind.

Whether nopixel will have its own GTA 6 RP server remains to be seen, but it would be surprising if Rockstar abandoned this side of the game when entering the next era. If this is just the beginning of a long term collaboration, GTA 6's online could be extremely special.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: New Street Fighter Trailer Teases Conflict Between Ryu and Ken, and E. Honda Does His Hundred Hand Slap
items.description: Legendary has dropped a new trailer for the Street Fighter movie showing E. Honda pulling off some of his iconic moves and teasing some unexpected tension between Ryu and Ken.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Legendary has dropped a new trailer for the Street Fighter movie showing E. Honda pulling off some of his iconic moves and teasing some unexpected tension between Ryu and Ken.

Street Fighter is hurricane kicking its way to theaters on October 16, and a new trailer has been shown in the lead-up to its release that features some of the game’s core cast members throwing down in familiar locales.

One of the more notable fighters who got some time to shine in this trailer was E. Honda, who we see facing off against Ryu in his famous bath house stage. He pulls off his Sumo Headbutt move (and surprisingly, it doesn’t look totally absurd), as well as his Hundred Hand Slap. For a moment, it looks like Ryu is on the losing end of this fight before he sends Honda flying with a Tatsumaki.

We also get to see Ryu and Ken brawling in a dark alleyway, and it seems like these two have had a falling out at some point, likely spurred by Ryu dropping off the face of the earth to pursue a path that appears to involve the Dark Hadou. We see him charging up a purple fireball as he says there was “darkness growing” within him — while Ken tries and fails to release a single Hadouken in his swanky apartment.

“I spent years living in Ryu’s shadow,” Ken says, promising to “win it all” at the World Warrior tournament thrown by M. Bison, who secretly plans on stealing the strongest fighters’ powers for himself (or something to that effect).

Chun-Li informs Ryu that Ken is in danger and urges him to "fight" and save him, though we aren’t sure of the specifics just yet. Could this be a parallel to the animated 1994 movie, where Bison captures Ken, brainwashing and transforming him into Violent Ken?

Cody Rhodes also gets some time to shine as Guile, who, in this movie, is a sarcastic, smart-mouthed guy as opposed to his stoic in-game counterpart. He delivers a few funny lines, one of which sees him interacting with Andrew Schulz’s Dan Hibiki.

Notably, Roman Reigns also makes an appearance as Akuma, lifting up Alexander Volkanovski’s Joe with the power of the Satsui no Hadou.

All in all, there’s a lot to chew on and break down in this trailer. Multiple characters are shown in various shots throughout the nearly three-minute-long clip, including Vega (Orville Peck), Balrog (50 Cent), Cammy (Mel Jarnson), and many more.

Street Fighter hits theaters on October 16. For more news on this adaptation of Capcom’s iconic fighting game series, check out our interview with David Dastmalchian at San Diego Comic-Con, where he told us all about how he dove deep into the minds of historic cult leaders to bring M. Bison and Shadaloo to life.

items.title: Ever Wanted to Sleep Inside a Giant Pokéball? In Japan, You'll Soon Have a Chance
items.description: What is it actually like inside a Pokéball? In Japan, you'll soon be able to find out.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
One of the biggest questions I've always had about Pokémon (and I have quite a few) is this: what is it actually like inside a Pokéball?

If memory serves correctly, the Pokémon anime series has occasionally shown a Pokéball's interior, with a miniaturized creature lounging inside. But I've always wondered how comfortable this is, and what if a Pokémon is claustrophobic? And why aren't there any windows?

Despite all of this, if someone told me I could go experience what living inside a Pokéball was like, I'd still likely take them up on the offer. And this is why I'm particularly intrigued by an upcoming collaboration between nap-tracking app Pokémon Sleep and the luxury Japanese hospitality firm Not a Hotel.

In a nutshell: you will be able to sleep inside a Pokéball soon.

このモンスターボール、本当に泊まれます。

◤￣￣￣￣￣
『Pokémon Sleep』✖️ NOT A HOTEL
　#泊まれるモンスターボール
　宿泊キャンペーン開催決定！
　　　　　　　　　　＿＿＿＿＿◢

詳細は9月15日（火）公開💤https://t.co/zdPHvAcAPa#ポケモンスリープ pic.twitter.com/habKvYosxT

— 【公式】ポケモン情報局 (@poke_times) September 1, 2026

A trailer for the experience reveals a giant spherical pod shaped like a half-open Pokéball, with its floor space largely taken up by a generous-sized spherical bed. And, yes, there is a window — though no curtains that I can see.

If you're intrigued to roleplay as a Pokémon and clamber inside a giant ball, then you'll want to keep an eye on the upcoming lottery (of course there's a lottery) on September 15 to secure your spot. You'll also need to travel to Hokkaido, Japan, where the Pokéball pod will be located, so do bear that in mind.

Prefer your bed without a giant perspex window, and also in your own house? That's fine too. And you'll have plenty of Pokéballs to throw in the next major entries in the Pokémon series, with Pokémon Winds and Waves on the way next year.

items.title: Ridley Scott Reportedly Says Paul Mescal Wasn't ‘Masculine Enough’ for Gladiator 2
items.description: Director Ridley Scott reportedly blamed Paul Mescal for Gladiator 2's underperformance, claiming the lead actor wasn't “masculine enough” for the role.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Director Ridley Scott reportedly blamed Paul Mescal for Gladiator II's underperformance, claiming the lead actor wasn't “masculine enough” for the role.

According to Puck News’ Matt Belloni (via World of Reel), this was the real reason why Mescal dropped out of Scott’s next film, The Dog Stars, and was replaced by Jacob Elordi.

Reports at the time claimed Mescal’s exit from The Dog Stars stemmed from scheduling conflicts with Sam Mendes’ four-part Beatles movie, where Mescal plays Paul McCartney.

IGN’s Tom Jorgensen, for one, appreciated Mescal’s performance, writing in his positive Gladiator II review that “Paul Mescal is adept in the belabored-hero role, going toe-to-toe with not only the delightfully deranged Joseph Quinn and Fred Hechinger, but also with Denzel Washington.”

While Gladiator II earned $462 million worldwide, the long-awaited sequel to the 2000 Best Picture winner also cost anywhere from $250 million to north of $300 million to produce.

The Dog Stars is one of the biggest box office flops of Ridley Scott’s career, opening to just $19 million worldwide on what was reportedly an $89 million budget.

In other Ridley Scott shit-talking news, the director recently said he’s developing a sequel to Alien: Covenant with Michael Fassbender because he thinks the Fede Alvarez-directed Alien: Romulus was just “OK” and the franchise “needs some help.”

Also be sure to read IGN’s picks for Ridley Scott’s 10 best movies, a list that doesn’t include Gladiator II, The Dog Stars, or Alien: Covenant.

items.title: Godzilla Dev Wants to Do More Remasters, But 'a Lot of Conversations' Need to Happen First
items.description: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is the only remaster Pipeworks can confirm for now, but "a lot of stuff is on the table," and there are "a lot of conversations to be had" in the future.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is the only remaster Pipeworks can confirm for now, but "a lot of stuff is on the table," and there are "a lot of conversations to be had" in the future.

The developer behind the November upgrade and the 2002 game it's based on opened up about the potential for more games in the series during an all-encompassing interview with IGN. With Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee officially coming back, the natural question we and everyone else had is: Will we be getting remasters for Godzilla: Save the Earth and Godzilla: Unleashed?

According to senior designer Simon Strange, it's too soon to say, but that doesn't mean he isn't rooting for it to happen.

"Let me tell you, I had that desire long before we announced this game, so I get it," Strange said. "I want to do all that stuff, too. I mean, all that stuff is now technically possible."

Strange said a Pipeworks engineer recently created a tool that allowed them to bring old assets out of their original Spigot engine and into Unreal, thus resulting in Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered. He confirmed the same technology could be used to create upgraded re-releases for the rest of the studio's arena fighter trilogy, too. Unfortunately, the studio hasn't signed any relevant contracts with publisher Atari just yet.

When Pipeworks launched its original Godzilla game for GameCube in 2002, the team only consisted of about "12 people in one room." The company has since ballooned to include around 300 people who are often spread across dozens of different projects at any given time. That includes more focused games like Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered, as well as titles it's served as co-developer on, like Marathon, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Concord, and Destiny 2.

Choosing how to allocate those resources isn't simple, and whether the demand for more Godzilla remasters is even there remains to be seen. Atari and Pipeworks have nothing to announce, even if Strange loves "the idea of bringing all that content back to the players." items.title: Tomb Raider Series Broke UK Crew Safety Laws, Report Confirms, Months After Star Sophie Turner Injured in Separate Incident
items.description: Amazon MGM Studios' new Tomb Raider series broke health and safety laws during production, just months after filming had to be halted due to star Sophie Turner's on-set injury.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Amazon MGM Studios' new Tomb Raider series broke UK health and safety laws during production, it's emerged, just months after filming had to be halted due to star Sophie Turner sustaining an injury on set.

In a separate incident, the production was found to have failed its "biological monitoring" duties regarding the use of potentially hazardous chemicals — isocyanate paints, which can cause asthma attacks.

Isocyanate paints require appropriate equipment to be worn during use and must be handled by properly protected staff, with the air then given up to 20 minutes to clear afterwards. Deadline reports that this was not adhered to on the Tomb Raider set, and the UK's Heath and Safety Executive (HSE) was forced to intervene.

The production was later confirmed to have broken the Health and Safety At Work Act 1974 and Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002. Despite the UK's non-stop use as a filming destination, just four HSE interventions have taken place over the past four years, making this a noteworthy occurrence — particularly for such a high-profile series.

Earlier this year, an on-set injury forced the entire production to be suspended for two weeks while Turner underwent treatment. The former Game of Thrones star is understood to have suffered a back injury, though healed sooner than some had feared. Meanwhile, the show's crew was reportedly paid for the time spent on hiatus.

Filming for Turner's Tomb Raider series initially began in January, with a starry cast that includes British acting legend Celia Imrie, Harry Potter star Jason Isaacs, as well as Alien and Avatar icon Sigourney Weaver. One unannounced cast member has also been spotted filming — former Lara Croft voice actress Keeley Hawes, who many fans suspect will play Lara's mother Amelia, in a neat passing of the torch from the video game series.

Tomb Raider is set to be released on Prime Video, though currently lacks a release date.

Image credit: Amazon MGM Studios

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Beta Extended
items.description: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 developer Infinity Ward has announced that the playable beta for the next first-person shooter in the long-running franchise has been extended until 10pm PT tonight/1am ET tomorrow morning.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 developer Infinity Ward has announced that the playable beta for the next first-person shooter in the long-running franchise has been extended until 10pm PT tonight/1am ET tomorrow morning.

"A little more time on the clock," the studio posted on its X account. We see you grinding out those Beta Rewards and camos, so we’re giving you some extra time. The #MW4 Open Beta is extended until 10 PM PT tonight. 2XP + Double Weapon XP stay active until close. Enjoy!"

Infinity Ward has already updated the beta, most recently to address TTK criticisms and tweak the weapons, but they also pushed changes out to beta testers last week as well.

It's been an unusual beta this year in the sense that a fan-favorite character's haircut has been the subject of some controversy, and the beta also included a single-player mission for the first time ever.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is due out on October 23 (although for those that preorder, you'll get access to the campaign on October 16) for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2, though it won't be included in Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on day one this year.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

items.title: New American Horror Story 13 Poster and Plot Teases Revealed
items.description: Ryan Murphy's dark and disturbing series - drops a new poster, episode titles and short synopses for installments 4-6.
items.author: Rachel Weber
items.content:
Someone over at Hulu decided to lock in on the social media campaign for American Horror Story 13 — the latest in Ryan Murphy's dark and disturbing series — dropping a new poster, episode titles and short synopses for installments 4–6.

The poster is classic Murphy, featuring a figure in a full black latex gimp suit, brandishing a giant black sunflower. Several characters have rocked the outfit — also known as the Rubber Man costume — throughout previous seasons, most notably Tate Langdon (played by Evan Peters in American Horror Story: Murder House).

That makes sense, as Murphy told Vogue that 13 would see some of the show's most popular characters return. "I just thought the number 13 was infused with so much stuff in the horror genre, and I wanted to do a greatest hits season," Murphy said.

The episode titles listed are:

  1. 13
  2. 1:13AM
  3. Rauhnacht
  4. Is That All There Is?
  5. Date Night
  6. The Return of Devils Night
  7. The Baddest Witch of Them All
  8. Hell No
  9. The Devil Is In the Details
  10. The Prodigal Son
  11. Madison’s Happy Ending
  12. Sisters in Arms
  13. Devil of a Good Time

Meanwhile, the plot teases for each are a sexy ankle flash of the horrible delights that await in episodes 4–6.

American Horror Story 13 will premiere just in time for spooky season, on FX on September 24, 2026.

items.title: Project Hail Mary Is Getting a VR Game This Fall
items.description: A new chapter from the world of Project Hail Mary is being released as a VR game this fall.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
A new chapter from the world of Project Hail Mary is being released as a VR game this fall.

Developer Maze Theory is producing a new VR/mixed reality title known as Project Hail Mary: Journey Among the Stars, which will tell an original new story in the sci-fi world. Players will step into the shoes of Ryland Grace (who appears to be a silent protagonist this time around) and work together with Rocky to diagnose and solve problems on your ship. It's unclear how long this game will be or how expansive it is, but it looks like a fun way for fans to get more Project Hail Mary content (and more Rocky).

The game will see actor James Ortiz reprising his role as the voice of Rocky, who expressed a lot of excitement in returning to the character for this game.

“Playing Rocky again for the game has been really special," said Ortiz. "Fans will be able to step inside the world of Project Hail Mary, interact with Rocky using the same character model from the film, and experience a completely new part of his journey with Grace. It is as close as you can get to the cinematic experience, but this time you are inside it.”

Project Hail Mary is one of the breakout successes from Hollywood this year, proving people are hungry for well-made original films. The movie grossed $684 million at the box office and became a viral sensation on platforms like TikTok. Although there's nothing officially in the works as far as we know, a sequel is on the table and likely in demand from Amazon. However, it falls on author Andy Weir to produce one, and it's unclear if that will happen or what it would even look like.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: No Rest for the Wicked 1.0 Launch Delayed to March 2027
items.description: No Rest for the Wicked developer Moon Studios has delayed the game's long-awaited 1.0 launch until March 2027.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
No Rest for the Wicked developer Moon Studios has delayed the game's long-awaited 1.0 launch until March 2027.

The news was confirmed today alongside a fresh trailer for the game, and an explanation that the wait would bring improved gameplay performance, a tightened class system and further polish to make the action RPG finally hit version 1.0 at "the standard it deserves."

If it feels like we've been waiting a long time for No Rest for the Wicked version 1.0, then that's because its initial PC early access build arrived back in April 2024. When the game does hit 1.0 in March 2027, it will do so for PlayStation 5 and PC. Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox Series X/S versions are still planned, but lack a formal launch date.

As a reward for players' patience, the game's Founders Pack of extra in-game items has been extended to anyone who purchases the game before January 1, 2027, with recent purchases now retroactively included in the offer. That's for PC players, to be clear, while PS5 pre-order customers will get a similar offer early next year.

"Let me apologize," said Moon Studios' Thomas Mahler in a video published today. "I hope you folks understand that this is huge passion project of ours. We have been working on the first prototypes for No Rest of the Wicked since 2016. We'd just like to take this extra time to make sure that we land this plane safely and that we don't ship with any silly little bugs left."

Mahler previously blamed the lesser-powered Xbox Series S for the game's Xbox Series version taking longer to launch.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: The Big Warrior Cats: Clans of the Forest Interview: Release Date, Clan Roles, Combat, and More
items.description: We got to speak with one of the developers behind Warrior Cats: Clans of the Forest, who opened up about the team’s creative process and what it’s like bringing the Clans to life.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Erin Hunter’s Warrior Cats franchise is finally getting an officially licensed video game coming to all major platforms this fall. We got to speak with one of the developers behind the turn-based title, who opened up about the team’s creative process and what it’s like bringing the Clans to life.

As a lifelong fan of the Warrior Cats world, I couldn’t believe it when I got the chance to quiz the developers at Bamtang Games and the folks at Coolabi Group about Clans of the Forest, the upcoming turn-based role-playing game based on the four original clans of the Warriors book series.

I also get to be the one to happily break the news of its official launch date. Warrior Cats: Clans of the Forest will release on October 23, 2026 on PC (Steam), PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, Nintendo Switch, and Nintendo Switch 2.

With that out of the way, let’s take a dive into my conversation with Adam Johnston, Creative Director at Bamtang Games, who assured me that his team is doing everything they can to stay true the the books’ lore — even to the point of bringing in community members to keep them on the right path.

IGN: The Warriors books are beloved by generations of fans. How does it feel being honored with the task of bringing this world to life?

Adam Johnston: Looking at the sheer scale of the world Erin Hunter built was a little intimidating at first. Once you realize just how many books, characters, and Clan dynamics exist, you understand the size of the mountain you're climbing. But as soon as our team jumped into the stories, that intimidation turned into excitement. We fell in love with the lore. Bringing it to life became a dream project for us. To make sure we get every detail right, we’ve had dedicated super fans working alongside us throughout development. They keep us honest and make sure we don't accidentally violate any sacred Clan traditions along the way. Having their feedback paired with our team's energy has been amazing. Our goal has been to craft something deeply authentic for readers who grew up with the series, while making it just as engaging for someone discovering Warriors for the first time. It's a huge responsibility, but we couldn't ask for a better world to build. If we have accidentally messed up the etiquette of a Gathering, we fully expect StarClan to strike us down.

IGN: Tell me a little bit about the production process for Clans of the Forest. Why a turn-based RPG? Was any inspiration taken from the Roblox game?

Adam Johnston: When you look at combat in the books, it isn't just cats slashing wildly at each other. It’s about stealth, positioning, and working as a team. A turn-based RPG made the most sense because it forces you to think strategically instead of just mashing buttons. It also let us build proper team battles and gives us a solid framework to make fights against badgers, foxes, or rival patrols actually work mechanically. Designing RPG combat for cats meant ditching standard spells. Instead, depth comes from shifting combat Stances. Every move you make alters your stance mid-fight, turning battles into a tactical game of reading your opponent and predicting their next move before they strike. As for Roblox, tons of respect to that community. They showed everyone years ago just how badly fans wanted to roleplay in this world. We're building a structured RPG rather than an open sandbox, but seeing their success gave us a lot of confidence that the appetite was definitely there.

IGN: Why did you make the choice to let players create their own cat, rather than play through the story as one of the established cats in the series?

Adam Johnston: If you ask almost any Warriors fan, the first thing they did after reading the books was figure out what their own warrior name would be and which Clan they belonged to. Self-expression is a huge part of why people fall in love with this universe in the first place. If we forced you to play as Firestar or another established character, you’d just be running through a story where you already know how everything turns out. Letting players create their own cat completely changes the game. It gives you incredible replayability, because every new cat you make comes with a different Clan, look, stat setup, and personality. Over time, you aren't just playing a single campaign. You're building your own personal legacy across the forest, populating the world with your own web of stories, rivalries, and characters across multiple playthroughs.

IGN: How important was cat customization to you? (As a kid who absolutely designed their own Warrior Cat OC, believe me, I get the appeal. Haha!)

Adam Johnston: Everyone who read these books had a notebook somewhere filled with their own custom cat designs. We knew if we didn't give players deep customization, we'd be missing the entire point of making a Warriors game. We wanted to make sure you could customize initial visuals like pelt patterns and eye colors, but also see your cat change as they get older. Your cat will start out as a cute apprentice and eventually end up looking like a grizzled veteran who has seen way too many badgers. On top of that, we tied identity directly into mechanics. Your Clan, level, and training shape your base stats, while the choices you make along your journey determine the moves you learn. That way, your cat actually grows up and lives a different story in the forest each time.

IGN: Will players get to choose certain roles, like being a Medicine Cat? Why or why not?

Adam Johnston: We anchored the player's path in the warrior ranks because every Clan needs a clear leader to face the prophecy, and we wanted the player to be that hero. While being a Medicine Cat is a fantasy for a lot of fans, their duty in the lore is healing and spiritual guidance, not tactical dueling or Clan leadership. The emotional climax across all four Sagas relies on you standing at the head of your Clan during its most dangerous hour. To give players a Hero's Journey, we wanted your choices to directly affect Clan politics and leadership. That said, Medicine Cats still play an important role in your journey. They are central to the story, spiritual guidance, and survival of your Clan, even if you aren't the one dispensing catmint yourself.

IGN: The Warriors books are known for being quite brutal, despite their young audience. Was the inclusion of any blood and gore discussed for this game?

Adam Johnston: We discussed this early on because the books are famous for their fierce battles. But for us, it wasn't about showing blood, it was about honoring the resilience of a warrior. We designed stylized visual scars that feel earned after tough encounters, avoiding anything graphic or scary. Giving players a toggle to turn those scars on or off in the settings was a crucial decision for us: it respects different age groups, sensory comfort, and player agency without diluting the dramatic tension of big important fights.

IGN: Is any DLC planned after the game's launch?

Adam Johnston: Right now, we are focused on the launch of the game. Any updates or plans for additional content will be addressed later.

IGN: And finally, do you have a message to the fans about what they can expect from Clans of the Forest?

Adam Johnston: The books don't pull punches. You've got dog packs, vicious badger fights, and some genuinely heavy character deaths. We knew we couldn't make a sanitized version of the forest, because treating this universe with respect means honoring those actual stakes. items.title: 'Did You Destroy My Favorite Game?': How the Heroes of Might and Magic 3 Community Is Guiding Ubisoft’s Reboot
items.author: Rachel Weber
items.content:
Ubisoft just revealed a remake of 1999's Heroes of Might and Magic 3 at Gamescom, and one look at the trailer shows it goes far beyond a simple polish and port. Set to release in 2027 across console and PC, the new game will swap the original's isometric 2D view with a 3D world and add new content - a fresh prologue campaign and some fancy cinematics - and tweak the original mechanics to make the game more accessible, without diluting the gameplay.

IGN spoke to Jean-Felix Monin, Creative Director at Ubisoft China, about the project and how the still very dedicated Heroes of Might and Magic 3 fanbase has been a key part of shaping this new version.

"I would say for us, the intention behind this game was really, there's this community, there's this great game that people have been kind of asking for a remake of for years now, and so we really want to do right by them," he said.

"We had contact with some key people in the community, people that we had worked with on other transmedia stuff, such as the board game, people that we knew we trusted and were quite representative and well-known, and they came and did some consulting."

This helped the team navigate some of the big changes, like the huge change from 2D isometric to 3D, complete with dynamic weather and seasons, and served as a north star for any gameplay changes. "So, the goal for us was to be really clear on the gameplay first. The gameplay is considered a masterpiece. And it's true that when you play the game, you really realize that, oh, wow, it's magical," said Monin.

"We took the decision really early on to not touch the gameplay. So, all the systems, all the balancing, had to stay exactly the same. We thought that through that, that would actually also address the question of, 'Okay, did you destroy my favorite game?'" he explained.

"We couldn't destroy it because we didn't touch it. That part we really didn't touch. And then on top of that, it was really, 'What can we do without touching this to make sure that we bring more value?' So the graphics, obviously, and also some quality of life features that we've added to make sure that modern players wouldn't feel too lost, because it's still kind of a unique type of gameplay, and so it might be a bit of a gap for people to get into it."

He also explained the decision to add a new prologue campaign. "There were kind of two reasons why we came with this idea," he said. "One was there was a lack of a good tutorial, so the original game just like threw you in. So you have the manual, so I guess people in the day were okay to read the book to understand about the game, but this is not something people do too much now."

"And there had been a tutorial made before, but that wasn't great. So we really thought there was a real need to teach this game to new players. So, this is something we needed to take the time to create. At the same time, there were a bit of loose ends, I would say, that are non-clear in the narrative about what happens before Catherine gets to Erathia and to Antagarich, and we thought that could be a good moment actually to mesh both together, because it's the first thing you play, and so that kind of eases you into the story and the gameplay at the same time."

The original Heroes of Might and Magic 3 scored a 9 on IGN when it was released, with our review calling it a triumphant return for the series and urging players old and new to give it a shot. "If you've already bought and played Heroes of Might and Magic I and II, you'll definitely be happy with 3. And if you're new to this series, pick this one up and give it a try."

Monin had a similar hope. "I think the goal is for us to really talk to the fans with nostalgia, to really get the feeling that they had 20-plus years ago," he said. "And then from there, we think by proxy, there could be a lot of new people coming in."

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

items.title: Nvidia's DLSS 5 Neural Rendering Tech Officially Launches on September 3, Hits Performance by Around 50–60%
items.description: Just last week, Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 technology leaked when a DLL file was found in the NBA 2K27 beta. It shouldn't be too surprising, then, that the technology will be officially launching on September 3 in, well, NBA 2K27.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Just last week, Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 technology leaked when a DLL file was found in the NBA 2K27 beta. It shouldn't be too surprising, then, that the technology will be officially launching on September 3 in, well, NBA 2K27.

Nvidia bills DLSS 5 as a 3D-bound neural rendering technique, which takes geometry and color data from the game you're playing, and then draws an AI-generated image on top of the rendered frame. The goal is to maximize photorealism, without the massive computational cost that would require in more traditional methods. Nvidia insists that because the model is constrained by the geometry and color information in the original scene, that it won't add extra elements to the scene or misplace objects. But that's something I'll have to test when the tech becomes available Thursday.

Regardless of the aesthetic changes that DLSS 5 has in games, it doesn't come for free. While some of the mods that materialized after the leak on Friday had some massive performance hits, I assumed that was partly because of a lack of optimization. However, even according to Nvidia, enabling the DLSS 5 neural renderer in NBA 2K27 will hit performance by around 50–60%. Although, it will have a noticeable impact on how the game looks.

To offset that performance hit, Nvidia encourages folks to enable the other parts of the DLSS software suite, like super resolution and frame generation to keep your frame rate high. The technology will also only work on RTX 5000 graphics cards at launch, but I'd recommend only enabling it if you have an RTX 5070 or better.

You can, of course, lower graphics settings or resolution to give yourself more leeway, but according to Nvidia, the better the source, the better the final image is going to look. I'm not sure what minimum graphics settings at a low resolution will do to the final image once DLSS 5 actually launches, but that's definitely something I'm going to test later this week.

Regardless, while DLSS 5 has had a controversial lead up to its release, I've definitely seen plenty of people in my own comments who think it makes games look much better. And now that it's going to be officially supported in a game by its developers we'll finally be able to see it in action beyond Nvidia's own marketing – and I know I'm excited to see exactly what it can do, and where it falls short.

Jackie Thomas is the Hardware and Buying Guides Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra
